scenes.title: 2015 University of Reading Lab: Chewing Gum Beats Finger-Tapping at Silencing Keypress Earworms
scenes.era: 2015, School of Psychology laboratory, University of Reading, UK

layout.description: Sunlit British cognitive lab bench with studio headphones, a mechanical computer keyboard logging earworm intrusions, and a side-by-side comparison of unwrapping a foil stick of gum versus rhythmic finger-tapping.

positions.who: 46-year-old adult participant in smart knit crewneck and collared shirt
positions.where: lifting studio headphones off ears, unwrapping a silver foil stick of gum, and chewing briskly while right hand rests calmly off the spacebar

positions.who: Philip Beaman in crisp tweed blazer holding Experiment 1–3 comparison clipboard
positions.where: standing beside the testing desk pointing to the 33% drop in earworm keypresses during gum chewing vs finger-tapping
positions.facing: observing the gum-chewing participant and monitor

props.name: silver foil pack of plain chewing gum beside studio headphones
props.period_detail: exact articulatory motor-interference prop from Beaman, Powell & Rapley (2015)
props.physical_behavior: State-A participant pulls headphones off ears and unwraps foil gum stick -> State-B rhythmic jaw chewing silences sub-vocal chorus loop

props.name: desktop mechanical spacebar counter logging 3-minute earworm intrusions
props.physical_behavior: State-A finger taps spacebar repeatedly during no-gum chorus intrusions -> State-B hand rests relaxed beside keyboard as count drops by 33%

actions.verb_sequence: pulls off studio headphones after a catchy 124-bpm chorus -> winces tapping spacebar on looping replays -> unwraps a stick of gum and chews steadily -> spacebar taps drop by a third
compares gum-chewing vs finger-tapping keypress logs on clipboard

reactions.reaction: raises eyebrows amazed that busy jaw muscles switched off a song inside the head
confirms inner speech-motor planning keeps earworms alive

scenes.wardrobe: Charcoal merino crewneck over white shirt; researcher in British academic navy blazer.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key Reading laboratory window daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Tapping your fingers barely dents a stuck song — yet chewing a stick of plain gum jams your inner vocal loop and cuts earworm replays by a third!

key_visual.description: a sunlit University of Reading lab where an adult removes studio headphones, unwraps a foil stick of gum, and chews while earworm keypresses drop on a desktop tally counter

scenes.title: Outdoor Morning Sidewalk Walk: How 124-BPM Songs Lock Onto Human Walking Tempo
scenes.era: Modern sunlit city sidewalk outside a corner cafe (Outdoor)

layout.description: Crisp sunlit morning street outside a corner bakery where a 50-year-old commuter steps onto the sidewalk carrying coffee as an upbeat 124-bpm cafe radio chorus locks right onto their brisk walking stride.

positions.who: 50-year-old commuter in trench jacket holding takeaway coffee cup
positions.where: striding briskly down a sunlit tree-lined sidewalk in exact 124-bpm rhythm
positions.facing: walking forward along sunlit outdoor sidewalk

props.name: takeaway coffee cup and pocket mint-gum pack
props.physical_behavior: State-A steps briskly in rhythm with cafe speaker -> State-B pulls gum pack from coat pocket to break the loop

actions.verb_sequence: exits cafe door at brisk walking tempo -> catches self humming the same 10-second hook -> reaches for pocket gum

reactions.reaction: chuckles catching the third repeat of the exact same chorus line

scenes.wardrobe: Tailored tan walking coat, navy scarf, leather shoes.
scenes.recognition_hook: Songs near 124 beats per minute hijack your brain because they match the natural cadence of human walking.

scenes.title: Evening Kitchen Dish-Washing Loop & Spoken Crossword Reset

layout.description: Warm home kitchen sink where rinsing dinner plates on autopilot triggers a stuck tune, promptly cleared by chewing gum or reading clues aloud.

positions.where: drying hands with a dish towel and reading a short newspaper anagram aloud to engage Broca's speech loop

props.name: dish towel, mint gum tin, and folded evening crossword
props.physical_behavior: State-A sets rinsed plate in rack -> State-B pops one mint gum piece and reads clue aloud

actions.verb_sequence: finishes rinsing plate -> chews mint gum for two minutes to clear the mental jukebox before bed

scenes.recognition_hook: Occupy your silent vocal muscles for two minutes and the mental jukebox lets go.
